newsitem.title: USA: Conrail falls as rival suitors hold talks.
newsitem.headline: Conrail falls as rival suitors hold talks.

text.p: Conrail Inc's share price tumbled in early trading Monday on fears that its rival suitors, CSX Corp and Norfolk Southern Corp, may negotiate an agreement for the acquisition of the Philadelphia-based railroad instead of waging a bidding war.
CSX and Norfolk Southern announced today that they were holding talks about their takeover offers for Conrail.
"This is not a good time to be having a long, drawn-out fight," said analyst Anthony Hatch of NatWest Securities. "The quicker they get to this, the better."
Shares of CSX were up 2-1/8 to 45-1/8 and Norfolk Southern stock was up 1-1/8 to 90-5/8.
CSX last month announced an agreement to acquire Conrail in a stock and cash deal valued at $92.50 per Conrail share.
A short time later, Norfolk Southern launched its own $100-per-share bid for Conrail.
Conrail has said it will review the Norfolk Southern offer.
CSX said it was discussing with Norfolk Southern the possible sale of assets after a CSX-Conrail merger.
Norfolk Southern said only that the discussions signaled its commitment to provide strong East Coast competition.
No further details on the talks were not disclosed.
A source familiar with the companies said Norfolk Southern initiated the talks with CSX late last week.
The negotiations mark a significant turnaround for both CSX and Norfolk Southern, which are locked in a court battle over their rival bids for Conrail.
"My hope is that there will be a three-way deal," said analyst Steve Lewins of Gruntal & Co.
